characters.name: Mother Serafine
characters.role: High Cleric of the Pale Light
characters.description: Head of the Church and its vast charitable apparatus. An older woman of immense spiritual authority and quiet political acuity. Serafine has held the Church together across three crises by knowing when to speak and when to vanish. She believes the city is one failed ward away from catastrophe — and acts accordingly, maintaining alliances no one knows she has.
characters.notes: Friendly to anyone containing the blight. Suspicious of Runeward's competence. Will trade information for favors she can document as charitable.

characters.name: Captain Edith Vaan
characters.role: Captain of the Order of the Pale Seal
characters.description: Commander of the Church's demon-hunters. Vaan is a compact, scarred woman who smells faintly of sulfur-compound solvents used in blight containment. She is relentlessly pragmatic — she will work with criminals if that's what contains the threat. Currently stretched thin managing both Ashfall and disturbing reports from the Drownways.
characters.notes: Willing to provide unofficial sanction for jobs that serve containment. Will remember if you make her life harder. Has intel on Old Nexus that she isn't sharing with Runeward.

characters.name: Prefect Alden Crane
characters.description: Commander of the city's law enforcement. A tall, meticulous man who came up through the courts rather than the streets. Crane understands law as a precision instrument — not a cudgel. He is deeply aware that his authority thins dramatically below Mid City and is quietly furious about it.
characters.notes: Responds to evidence, not pressure. Will not be bribed, but can be approached through proper channels. Hates the Night Market with professional intensity. Has a long memory for informants who proved reliable.

characters.name: Inspector Mira Solt
characters.description: One of the few Wardspire inspectors who regularly works the Lower City. Solt grew up in The Stacks and has a complicated relationship with her former neighbors. She's effective, occasionally bribeable with the right framing ("for the victim's family"), and knows every crew operating below the Mid City line.
characters.notes: Good source of Lower City intel for the right price. Has a case she can't officially pursue and might contract it out. Will not sanction violence against civilians — that's her hard line.

characters.name: Archmage Thessaly Corrin
characters.description: The city's supreme licensed magic authority. Corrin is brilliant and visibly anxious in a way that powerful people rarely allow themselves to show — because she knows the actual state of the ward network and it is worse than the public-facing reports. She is constantly calculating how long until something catastrophic requires a cover story.
characters.notes: Desperate for reliable contractors who can handle sensitive ward problems without filing official reports. Will pay well for discretion. Genuinely frightened of what's happening in Old Nexus.

characters.name: Archivist-General Voss
characters.description: Controls all legal identity in Aurelion. An unreadable, ink-stained bureaucrat who understands that his greatest power is the one he never exercises visibly. Voss can erase a person from the city's records with a single ledger correction. He has done this three times in the past decade. No one has found the pattern.
characters.notes: Will not be approached directly for record alteration — too dangerous for him. Has intermediaries for the right kind of request. Knows things about old noble families that would destroy them. That knowledge is for sale through complex channels.

characters.name: Guildmaster Bram Holt
characters.description: A broad-shouldered, self-made man who despises the old money of Stonefall and the idealists of the Stacks with equal vigor. Holt runs the guild federation through favors, contracts, and the threat of withdrawing labor from districts that don't cooperate. He is currently worried about the Stacks Collective and looking for ways to discredit Ela Stirn.
characters.notes: Will hire the crew for anti-Collective work if it can be made untraceable. Also vulnerable to labor law violations that could embarrass him publicly. Has a warehouse of off-books goods in Night Market that he'd like retrieved quietly.

characters.name: Director Orenna Cale
characters.description: Runs the only safe transit between the three surviving cities. Cale is professional, controlled, and intensely aware that her position depends on the rail lines remaining the only option. She is quietly investigating the Drownways Syndicate's alternate smuggling routes and has significant resources to deploy in that fight.
characters.notes: Good source for inter-city information and travel documentation. Will pay for intelligence on Drownways operations. Has the power to flag a person's travel record in ways that make leaving Aurelion difficult.

characters.name: The Collector
characters.description: No one knows the Collector's real name. They appear at specific pub tables on specific nights, settle disputes between crews, and manage the informal debt ledger that keeps Low Lanterns from erupting into full war. They dress like a minor merchant and speak like a retired schoolteacher. The violence in their employment is performed by others.
characters.notes: Approach with a specific debt dispute or a job offer — not with general inquiries. Will broker neutral meetings. Information about other crews' current activities is always welcome.

characters.name: Mama Rue
characters.description: An elderly woman who has run the same tea stall in the Night Market for forty years. She is everyone's grandmother and no one's fool. Rue mediates disputes between the market's family networks, extends credit with long memory, and knows every forger, folk healer, and unlicensed practitioner in the district by name. She is the closest thing the Night Market has to authority.
characters.notes: Approach with respect and a small gift — she notices. Will provide introductions to any Night Market specialist for the right reasons. Fiercely protective of her people; anything that harms the market's families becomes her problem.

characters.name: Ela Stirn
characters.description: An Elvish refugee who came to Aurelion three decades ago and never left. Stirn has spent those decades building something patient and dangerous: a mutual aid network with actual teeth. She leads through consensus and quiet persuasion. Guildreach considers her the single greatest threat to their labor model.
characters.notes: Hard to approach for a criminal crew — she doesn't trust people who profit from the same system that oppresses her people. Will work with the crew if the job clearly benefits the Stacks' residents. Absolutely will not be used against her own.

characters.name: Silent Henn
characters.description: Henn communicates entirely through written notes and a small number of trusted intermediaries. Whether this is a speech impediment, an affectation, or an operational security choice, no one outside the Syndicate knows. What everyone knows is that Henn's canal network is the most reliable smuggling route in Aurelion.
characters.notes: All dealings go through intermediaries first. Henn will not meet in person until trust is established across multiple jobs. Values reliability above coin — a crew that runs jobs cleanly is worth more than one that bids high and flakes.

characters.name: Lord Caspar Fell
characters.description: The head of the most indebted noble house in Stonefall, clinging to a title his grandfather purchased and a manor his father mortgaged twice. Fell is desperate, educated, and dangerous in the way that desperate educated men always are. He has made at least one deal with someone he should not have in order to reverse his family's decline.
characters.notes: Will hire the crew for sensitive jobs involving his family's interests — recovering compromising documents, dealing with creditors quietly, etc. Useful as a cover for Upper City access. The deal he made is still outstanding and will cause problems.

characters.name: The Dreamer
characters.description: Not quite a person. Something that sends visions — fragments of the Demon King's era, architectural plans for places that no longer exist, memories that belong to no one living. The Dreamer contacts sensitive individuals unprompted. What it wants is unclear. Whether it is trapped, testing, or recruiting is a question the Order of the Pale Seal has not been able to answer.
characters.notes: Does not respond to conventional approach. Appears in dreams following exposure to Old Nexus artifacts. The visions contain genuine information mixed with something that seems like bait. The GM should use this NPC carefully.

locations.name: Aurelion
locations.description: The former capital of a slain Demon Lord. Centuries ago a hero's party defeated the Demon King and liberated the land — then failed to build a stable peace. The land beyond the walls is blighted and unlivable. Aurelion survives not because it is healthy, but because it isolates its failures.
locations.notes: Height = legitimacy and safety. Movement between tiers is frictional. Old Nexus lies beneath everything.

locations.name: Aurelion City
locations.description: A vertically and morally layered city. 14 districts divided into Upper City, Mid City, Lower City, and Undercity. The defining belief: it is better to contain a problem than fix it.
locations.notes: Connected to two surviving cities via warded rail lines (Ironline). Most citizens never leave.

locations.name: Upper City
locations.description: Legitimacy, ideology, memory. The upper reaches of Aurelion where authority is performed and history is curated. Height equals safety here.

locations.name: Mid City
locations.description: Control, infrastructure, necessity. Where the law lives, magic is licensed, goods move, and labor is organized. The machinery of the city.

locations.name: Lower City
locations.description: Survival, crime, adaptation. Not "poor districts" — different survival mechanisms, each absorbing a different kind of pressure the city cannot resolve.

locations.name: Undercity
locations.description: The buried remnants of the Demon King's power. Old, sealed, not resolved. Those who go below often do not return the same.

locations.name: Crownrise
locations.description: Ceremonial power and public spectacle. Authority as theater. Parades, proclamations, and monuments to the Hero's party fill wide boulevards. Legitimacy is performed here daily.

locations.name: High Sanctum
locations.description: Faith, charity, demon-hunting, and moral oversight. The Church founded by the original Cleric. Grand cathedral, healing wards, and the Order of the Pale Seal — the city's sanctioned demon-hunters.

locations.name: Stonefall
locations.description: Decaying noble estates and the abandoned prison. Old power rots here. Ancient families cling to titles that carry less weight each decade. The prison has been sealed for thirty years.

locations.name: Archivum
locations.description: Records, identity, erasure. Reality is defined on paper here. The Archivum controls who exists legally in Aurelion — birth records, property deeds, licenses, and the quiet power to unmake a person by altering a ledger.

locations.name: Wardspire
locations.description: Courts, Bluecoat HQ, central prison. Law made concrete. The Wardspire enforces law across all tiers, though its presence thins in the Lower City and disappears entirely in the Drownways.

locations.name: Runeward
locations.description: Licensed magic, ward engines, inspections. The institution founded by the original Mage. Magic is infrastructure here — not wonder. Unlicensed casting is illegal; inspectors patrol ward maintenance across the city.

locations.name: Ironline
locations.description: Rail hub connecting Aurelion to the two other surviving cities. Movement is privilege. The warded rail lines pass through blighted wastes, making rail travel the only safe way out. Ironline controls that movement.

locations.name: Guildreach
locations.description: Industry, labor contracts, and controlled production. Where goods are made and labor is formally organized — and exploited. The Guilds set wages, working hours, and which trades are permitted in each district.

locations.name: Low Lanterns
locations.description: Pub district. Crews, street justice, social violence. The city's pressure-release valve for organized violence. Rival crews negotiate territory here. The Bluecoats make arrests when convenient, ignore problems when paid.

locations.name: Night Market
locations.description: Dense enclave. Gambling, family networks, pop-up stalls, folk healing, quiet crime. The city's unofficial commerce. Illicit goods move here. Family connections count for more than coin. Unlicensed magic is tolerated.

locations.name: The Stacks
locations.description: Vertical overcrowding. Labor reservoir. Elvish refugees in upper levels tend rooftop gardens and hold long memory and quiet resentment. The Stacks absorbs excess population the city cannot place elsewhere.

locations.name: Drownways
locations.description: Flooded low district. Canals, smuggling routes, waste transport. The city's waste and secrets flow through here. Canal networks connect to below-street passages. The Bluecoats rarely enter without reason.

locations.name: Ashfall
locations.description: Blight containment. Quarantine, failing wards, quiet suffering. Where the demon-king's corruption still seeps through. Church wardens maintain failing wards. Residents cannot leave without a health writ. The city's supernatural failure, contained.

locations.name: Old Nexus
locations.description: The buried heart of the Demon King's power. Sealed. Not resolved. Runeward's deepest wards hold here — barely. Treasure hunters, cultists, and the desperate venture below. Most don't come back unchanged.

factions.name: The Ruling Structure
factions.description: Symbolic authority descended from the original Hero. The seat of legitimate power — but mostly ceremonial. Actual decisions are brokered between the Church, Wardspire, and Runeward. The Ruling Structure legitimizes; it rarely commands.
factions.goals: Maintain the appearance of unified authority. Prevent any single institution from seizing full control.
factions.threats: Institutional drift rendering the ruling structure irrelevant. Public loss of faith in the Hero's legacy.

factions.name: High Sanctum
factions.description: The Church founded by the original Cleric. Controls faith, charity, moral oversight, and demon-hunting through the Order of the Pale Seal. Operates in High Sanctum and maintains a presence in Ashfall managing blight containment.
factions.goals: Moral authority over all institutions. Expand the Order of the Pale Seal. Keep Ashfall contained.
factions.threats: Failing wards in Ashfall. Runeward encroaching on supernatural jurisdiction. Loss of public faith.

factions.name: Wardspire
factions.description: Military order evolved from the original Commander's forces into the city's law enforcement. Bluecoats, courts, and the central prison. Enforces law everywhere — though unevenly. Power flows through punishment and the threat of it.
factions.goals: Maintain order through visible authority. Expand jurisdiction into areas that currently resist Wardspire presence.
factions.threats: Corruption within the Bluecoats. Night Market and Low Lanterns undermining authority. Political pressure from Guildreach.

factions.name: Runeward
factions.description: The magic-regulating institution founded by the original Mage. Controls licensed magic, ward engine maintenance, and inspections across all districts. Magic is infrastructure — not wonder — and Runeward controls the infrastructure.
factions.goals: Maintain monopoly on licensed magic. Expand ward coverage into failing areas. Suppress unlicensed practice.
factions.threats: Old Nexus leaking demon-corruption that overwhelms wards. Night Market's folk healers operating unlicensed. Runeward budget cuts.

factions.name: The Archivum
factions.description: Controls records, identity, and legal existence. Reality is defined on paper. The Archivum can erase a person — revoke citizenship, nullify property, expunge records. Quiet power. No armies needed when you control who exists.
factions.goals: Maintain control of identity infrastructure. Expand record-keeping to the Lower City. Commodify access to records.
factions.threats: Night Market forgers undercutting official documents. Political pressure to falsify records for powerful clients.

factions.name: Guildreach
factions.description: The guild federation controlling industry, labor contracts, and production quotas. Formally legitimate. Functionally exploitative. Draws labor from The Stacks and sets wages that keep workers dependent. Rivals Wardspire for mid-city influence.
factions.goals: Expand labor contracts into informal economies. Break Stacks Collective organizing. Secure preferred rail access through Ironline.
factions.threats: Labor unrest. Stacks Collective building power. Wardspire investigating guild bribery.

factions.name: Ironline Authority
factions.description: Controls the warded rail lines connecting Aurelion to the two surviving cities. Movement is privilege and Ironline controls that privilege. Rail passes, cargo inspection, and customs enforcement generate enormous revenue.
factions.goals: Maintain monopoly on inter-city transit. Increase rail-pass prices. Prevent smuggling that bypasses official cargo.
factions.threats: Drownways syndicate building smuggling routes that bypass customs. Blight expansion threatening rail ward integrity.

factions.name: Stacks Collective
factions.description: An informal labor organizing body centered in The Stacks, with growing support among elvish refugees. Quietly building mutual aid networks, strike funds, and a collective memory of grievance. Guildreach wants them destroyed.
factions.goals: Improve working conditions. Establish formal elvish representation. Build enough power to negotiate with Guildreach.
factions.threats: Wardspire infiltration. Guildreach pressure. Internal division between human labor and elvish factions.

factions.name: Low Lantern Crews
factions.description: Collective term for the rotating constellation of street crews that control territory in Low Lanterns. They manage extortion, debt collection, and street-level violence. Frequently at war with each other; occasionally united against outside threats.
factions.goals: Control more territory. Extract tribute from businesses. Avoid full Wardspire crackdowns.
factions.threats: Wardspire consolidation efforts. Rival crews. Night Market encroaching on their income streams.

factions.name: Drownways Syndicate
factions.description: Smuggling operation built around the canal networks of the Drownways. Moves illicit goods, provides underground transit, and handles waste disposal for parties that need discretion. Operates below Wardspire notice — mostly.
factions.goals: Expand canal routes. Establish a reliable channel into Old Nexus for artifact recovery. Avoid Wardspire crackdowns.
factions.threats: Ironline Authority lobbying for canal inspection rights. Old Nexus instability disrupting lower routes.

factions.name: Night Market
factions.description: The dense informal economy of the Night Market district. Family networks, forgers, folk healers, unlicensed magic practitioners, and quiet crime. Handles the unofficial problems the city cannot acknowledge. More stable than it looks.
factions.goals: Maintain independence from Wardspire and Runeward. Protect family networks. Quietly expand into Guildreach's blind spots.
factions.threats: Archivum cracking down on forged documents. Runeward inspectors raiding folk healers. Wardspire informants.

factions.name: Stonefall Houses
factions.description: The decaying noble families of Stonefall, clinging to old titles and older debts. Some dabble in forbidden deals — with Old Nexus, with Night Market, with anyone who can restore their fading influence. Individually weak; collectively unpredictable.
factions.goals: Restore political relevance. Recover lost estates. Access Old Nexus resources without anyone finding out.
factions.threats: Further decay. Younger families absorbing their assets. Wardspire investigating old crimes.

factions.name: Old Nexus
factions.description: Not a faction in the traditional sense — more a pressure. The sealed heart of the Demon King's power. Something still stirs below the wards. Cultists, relic hunters, and the desperate are drawn to it. What emerges from the Nexus rarely serves human interests.
factions.goals: Unknown. Expansion. Return. The wards hold — for now.
factions.threats: Runeward wards failing. Cultists accelerating whatever process is occurring below.

factions.name: Order of the Pale Seal
factions.description: The Church's demon-hunting order. Trained to detect, contain, and cleanse demonic corruption. Operates with religious authority above Wardspire in matters of blight and possession. Currently stretched thin between Ashfall and reports from the Drownways.
factions.goals: Contain Ashfall blight. Investigate Nexus-related incidents. Maintain Church authority over supernatural jurisdiction.
factions.threats: Overwhelmed by Ashfall's expansion. Political friction with Runeward over who has authority over demonic magic.
